translations.text: And King Josiah kept the Passover of the Lord in Jerusalem, and he offered the Passover sacrifice of the Lord on the fourteenth day of the first month.
And he organized the priests and appointed them in the house of the Lord according to the whole number of the days, and he clothed them in the priestly tunic.

And he said to the Levites, the ministers: "Sanctify yourselves and prepare yourselves according to the holiness of the ark of the covenant of the Lord in the temple that King Solomon, the son of David, built. And let no uncleanness or defilement be found among you.

"And now serve in the service of the Lord our God. Gather and prepare the whole nation of Israel, and arrange them according to the order of the patriarchs and of their tribes, as David, king of Israel, and his son, the great Solomon, ordained and wrote."
And the Levites stood in the temple according to the order, each according to his fathers, before their brothers, the children of Israel.
"And according to the former rite, offer the Passover sacrifice, prepare the offering, and keep the Passover according to the command of the Lord, as he commanded through Moses."
And Josiah granted and gave to the people thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand calves. He gave all this, according to the king's command, to the people, the priests and the Levites.
And then he gave two thousand six hundred sheep and six hundred calves to Hilkiah and Zechariah, the high priests and leaders of the people, and to the priests.
And Jeconiah, Shemaiah, his brother Nathanael, Hashabiah, Odel and Joram, the commanders of thousands, gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred calves for the Passover.
And the priests received all this with very great glory, and with all splendor they prepared the Passover of Unleavened Bread,
according to their tribes and according to their rites and their divisions.
The priests stood in their order before the congregation and offered the sacrifice to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses.
And so in the morning they prepared the Passover roasted with fire. They boiled the other offering with spices in pots and cauldrons, and they offered it for all the people.

And after this the high priests prepared themselves and their brothers, the sons of Aaron, because the priests were offering the fat for the burnt offering by fire. And the Levites prepared themselves and their brothers the priests, the sons of Aaron.

And the sons of Asaph, the chanters and singers, prepared themselves, as King David had ordained: Asaph, Zechariah and Eddinus. And the gatekeepers each kept watch at the gates, each according to their order of days, because their brothers the Levites had also prepared themselves.
And all together they completed the Passover of the Lord on that day, and they offered the sacrifice of the Lord on the altar according to the command of King Josiah.
And the children of Israel who were present at that time kept the Passover of the Lord and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
And such a Passover had never been kept in Israel, for no one had kept a Passover like it since the times of Samuel the prophet.
None of the kings of Israel ever held a Passover like the one that King Josiah held together with the priests, the Levites, the Jews and all Israel who were living in Jerusalem at that time.
This Passover took place in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
Josiah's deeds were upright before his Lord, and he served the Lord with all his heart and mind.
There were also other kings before him, about whom it is written that they sinned and became lawless among all the nations. They grieved the Lord and rose up to attack his words in Israel.
After all these righteous acts of Josiah, Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians, came to make war at Carchemish on the Euphrates. Josiah went out to fight him.
The king of the Egyptians sent word to him and said: "What is there between you and me, O king of Judea?
The Lord God has not sent me against you. I am going to make war on the Euphrates. Now the Lord is with me, so do not oppose the Lord."
But Josiah did not turn his chariots back. Instead he set about fighting him. He did not listen to the words of Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke to him from the mouth of the Lord.
Instead he gathered his forces and attacked Pharaoh in the plain of Edda. And the commanders came down against King Josiah.
King Josiah said to his servants: "Take me out of this battle, for I have become very weak." At once his servants carried him out of the battle.
He got up into his second chariot, and they brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried with his fathers.

All Judea wailed and mourned for Josiah. Jeremiah the prophet spoke this lament for Josiah. He sat with the women, and they lament with that lament of Jeremiah to this very day. They gave a command to their generations to lament always in Israel.

All this is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel: the deeds that Josiah did, the valour with which he fought, his great righteousness and glory, and the wisdom of his reverence, which he had through the law of the Lord. All of this the books of the kings of Israel and Judah tell to this day.
From his family they made Jeconiah, son of Josiah, king, and Jeconiah reigned in place of his father Josiah. He was twenty-three years old when he became king.
He reigned over Judea and Jerusalem for three months. Then the king of the Egyptians removed him, so that no one would reign over them.
He imposed on them a levy of a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold.
The king of the Egyptians appointed Jehoiakim, Jeconiah's brother, king over them, and Jehoiakim reigned over Judea and Jerusalem.
Jehoiakim imprisoned the nobles and the leaders of the house of Israel. And he brought his brother Zara out of the land of Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when they made him king over Judea and Jerusalem, and he did evil before the Lord.
In his days Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came up against him. He bound him in bronze fetters and took him away to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar took the vessels of the house of the Lord, carried them away and placed them in the house of his idols.
All of this about him, and about his lawlessness and his defilement, is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings.
And Joakim, his son, reigned in his place, and he was eighteen years old,
and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. And he did evil before the Lord.
And after one year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and carried him off to Babylon, together with the treasures of the house of the Lord;
and he set up Zedekiah as king over Judea and Jerusalem. Zedekiah was thirty years old, and he reigned eleven years.
And he did evil before the Lord. He did not turn back from his wickedness, nor did he listen to the words of Jeremiah the prophet, which he spoke to him from the mouth of the Lord,

and the oath that he had sworn to King Nebuchadnezzar in the name of the Lord: he did not keep that oath, but broke faith and turned away from Nebuchadnezzar. And he hardened his heart and his neck and transgressed the law of the Lord, the God of Israel.

And the leaders of the people and the priests committed much ungodliness and became lawless, and they multiplied their uncleanness beyond that of all the nations, and they defiled the temple of holiness of the God of Israel.
And God sent a prophet as messenger to their fathers, so that they might turn back, for he was sparing them and his temple of holiness.

But they despised his messengers. And on the day when the Lord spoke to them, they mocked his prophets. And the Lord was angered against that nation because of their ungodliness, and he sent the kings of the Chaldeans against them.

And they slew their young men with the sword and poured out their blood around the temple of holiness. And he did not spare their children and virgins and old men and young men, but delivered everything into their hands.

And all the vessels for the service of the Lord, great and small, and the vessels for the service of the ark of the Lord, and all the treasures of the kings of Israel, they took and carried off to Babylon.
And they burned the temple of the Lord with fire, and they tore down and laid waste the walls of Jerusalem, and burned its towers with fire.
And that was the end of all their glory. And the remnant they drove before them and carried captive to Babylon.
And they served them and their children until the kings of the Persians, in fulfillment of the word of the Lord which he spoke by the mouth of Jeremiah the prophet:

"Until the land is pleasing to the Lord." And he made it keep sabbath, empty, through all those times; as long as it lay desolate, it was reckoned to them as sabbath rest, until seventy years were fulfilled.

And in the reign of Cyrus over the Persians, in the first year, the word of the Lord which he spoke by the mouth of Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, and the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of the Persians, and Cyrus gave a command to all who were in his kingdom, and wrote and said:

"Thus says Cyrus, king of the Persians: The sovereign of all the ends of heaven, the Lord, the God of Israel, has revealed to me — the Lord has truly revealed to me — that I should build his temple in Jerusalem of Judea. In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, in the seventieth year from the captivity, Judah and Benjamin completed [?]. And in all Cyrus reigned seven years.

Now whoever there is who has with him any of the kindred of the Jews, may the Lord, the God of Israel, be with him; and let them go up to Jerusalem with those Jews and build the temple of the Lord, the God of Israel, for he is the Lord who dwells in Jerusalem.

And all who lived in their own places helped them with gold and silver, with horses and all kinds of livestock, and with everything they had prepared they made offerings to the temple of God in Jerusalem.

And the chiefs of the clans and the heads of families of the tribe of Judah and of the tribe of Benjamin stood up, along with the priests and the Levites and all those whose spirit the Lord had stirred to go and build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
And those who lived around them helped with gold and silver, with horses and livestock, and they made vows to the Lord, as much as came into each one's mind.
And King Cyrus had the holy vessels of the Lord brought out, which King Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and placed in the house of his idols.

Cyrus, king of the Persians, had them brought out and ordered the vessels to be given to Mithridates, his chief treasurer. Mithridates handed them over and gave them to Sanabassar, the governor of Judah.
And this was the number of the holy vessels of the Lord: a thousand gold vessels and a thousand silver vessels, twenty-nine silver censers,

thirty gold bowls [?] and two thousand four hundred and twenty silver ones. This is Cambyses, who reigned ten years, whom some call Artaxerxes the Short [?] [this sentence is garbled]. And a thousand other vessels.

All the vessels of gold and silver that were brought came to five thousand four hundred and sixty-nine. They gave all these into the hands of Sanabassar, and brought them out of Babylon together with all the captives and carried them up to Jerusalem.

In the time of the reign of Artaxerxes, king of the Persians, in the twenty-second [?] Artaxerxes [?], those who lived around Judea and Jerusalem wrote to him: Bishlam and Mithridates and Tabellius, and Rathumus and Beeltethmus and Samellius the scribe, and many others with them who lived along the seacoast: Canaanites and Tyrians, Ammonites and Moabites and Samaritans and many others, who governed the region. They wrote a letter as follows:
"To King Artaxerxes, our lord, from your servants: Rathumus, who bows down before you, and Samellius the scribe, and all our fellow counselors, and the judges of Assyria and of Canaan. We greet you.

Now let it be known to you, our lord and king, that the Jews who left you and came to us have arrived in Jerusalem, that city of rebels and troublemakers. They are building it up, they mean to strengthen its marketplaces and its walls, and they want to rebuild the temple.
Now if this city is built and its walls are finished, they will pay tribute to no one, and will even rise up to fight against kings.
For they boast in their temple and put their trust in it. So it seemed good to us that our lord the king should look into this matter. Search and see what your earliest forefathers wrote down,

and you will find the written records and learn that this city is a city of rebels, that its kings, the Jews, are rebels, and that its inhabitants have always broken their oaths. That is why this city was laid waste and became a desert.
Now we inform our lord, your Majesty, that if this city is built and its walls are raised up, you will no longer have authority or a road through the regions of Assyria and Canaan."
At that time King Artaxerxes wrote to Rathumus, to Beeltethmus, to Samellius the scribe and to all the others who lived in the regions of Samaria, Assyria and Canaan, who had written to him:
"I have read the letter that you wrote to me,

and I ordered the chronicles of the records to be searched. It was found that this city has been rebellious against all kings from the beginning up to now, and that the land is merciless [?]. Those who live in it have striven [?] in every way,
and mighty and fierce kings who lived in Jerusalem ruled and collected tribute from the regions of Assyria and Canaan.
Now, then, I have ordered that those men must not rebuild that city.
And you must take care that their wickedness does not grow any further, and that they do not rise up in rebellion and bring trouble on this kingdom of ours."
Then Rathumus and Samellius the scribe, and many others with them, read the letter of King Artaxerxes. They went up quickly to Jerusalem with horses and troops and did not allow the Jews to build.
And the building of the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem was halted until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of the Persians.
King Darius held a great celebration. He summoned all his princes, his children, and all the great men of the Medes, the Persians and the Chaldeans,
and with them all the lords, governors and rulers of the provinces. From India to Ethiopia there were one hundred and twenty-seven of these princes.
They ate and drank, were filled, and became merry. When it was evening, King Darius went into his bedchamber, got onto his bed and fell asleep.
At that time, while the king slept, his three chamberlains were guarding and keeping watch in the bedchamber. They began to talk with one another and said:

"Come, let each of us make one statement. Whoever speaks more wisely and more powerfully than his companions, King Darius will give him a great reward." Cyrus reigned thirty years, and another twelve years; Kais [?], nine; the Magus, one; Darius, two years. These are the years from the building of the house.

"He will exalt him and make him famous above everyone else. He will dress him in purple. He will eat and drink from golden vessels, and lie down and sleep on golden bedding. He will be mounted on a chariot with a golden bridle, a headdress of fine linen will be placed on him, a diadem will be bound on him, and a golden necklace will be put around his neck.
Because of his wisdom he will sit on the throne second to Darius, and he will be called a kinsman of Darius."
Then each of them wrote down his statement. They sealed them, put them under King Darius's pillow, and said:

"When he gets up, let us hand him this writing. The king and the princes of Persia will read it, and whoever's statement is found to be the wisest will be given the honour of victory." King Darius had held a great feast in the first year of his reign.
The first wrote: "Wine is strong, and mightier than everything!"
The second wrote: "Royal majesty is mighty, and stronger than everything!"
The third wrote: "Women are mighty and stronger than everything, but truth conquers all!"
When the king woke up, they brought the writing and gave it to the king, and he read it.

And he sent and summoned all the princes of Persia, the lords, the generals, the governors and the rulers. And he sat in the place where they had all gathered to him, and the writing was read aloud before them all.
And the king said, "Call those chamber-guards here, and let them explain their words to us." And when they had called them, they brought them in before the king.
And they said to them, "Tell us all of it."
And the first, the one who had spoken about the strength of wine, began to speak, and he said this:
"O men, how is wine not strong? It befuddles the minds of all the men who drink it.
It makes the minds of the king and of the poor man one and the same, and likewise of the master and the slave, of the rich and the needy.
It bends and turns the minds of everyone to joy, and they do not remember sorrow and pain.
It fills the minds of everyone with gladness and wealth. They do not remember kings and princes, and it deceives the very great.
And when a man gets drunk, he does not remember friends or brothers or enemies, and many times he even draws the sword.
And when it has passed off, he does not remember what he has done.
O men, how is wine not strong, when it compels men to do all this?" And when he had said all this, he fell silent.
And the second began to speak, the one who had spoken about the strength of kings:
"O men, are men not strong? Do they not hold the sea and the dry land and everything in them?
But kings rule with strength over the whole earth. The king speaks and commands, and they do it at once.

If he commands them to fight, comrade against comrade, they do not transgress his command. If he sends them into battle against enemies, they go at once, build their siege engines, and overthrow walls and towers.
They kill and are killed, and they do not transgress the king's command. And if they win, they bring every good thing to the king.

And not only the warriors drawn from the people, but also the laborers who work the land: when they sow and reap, they bring their produce to the king. And then the tax-collectors oppress the country and exact the royal tribute.
And the king alone, made strong, rules over it. If he orders them to kill, they kill; if he orders them to spare life, they spare it;
if he orders them to build, they build;
if he orders them to tear down, they tear down; if he orders them to plant, they plant.
And the whole world obeys the command of the king's power.

And whatever the king wishes, he does. He sits at ease in his treasure-house [?], and eats and drinks and sleeps. And all the others around him serve him and wait for his command. They are not free to go and act as they wish, and they do not dare to transgress the king's command.
Now, O men, how is the king not strong, when the word of his command rules over everyone with such strength?" When he had said this, he fell silent.
And the third, the one who had spoken about the strength of women and about truth (this is Zerubbabel), began to speak and said:
"O men, if the king is great, and so are many other men, and if wine is strong, who is it that has mastered and holds them, and rules over all of them? Is it not women?
For it is women who have borne kings and all the people who rule over sea and land.
From them were born, and by women were reared, the laborers who planted the vineyard, from which wine comes;
it is they who make clothing for men, and because of them men are adorned and glorified; and men cannot exist without them.
And if men gather gold and silver and every kind of abundance, and then see a beautiful woman, they turn to her, gape at her with open mouths and gaze at her.
And with all their will they love her more than gold, more than silver and more than every delight.
And a man leaves his own father and mother, who bore him and reared him, and his own country, and follows in the footsteps of his wife, and so cleaves to her,
and becomes of one soul with her. And he does not remember his father, or his mother, or his country.
And from this you must know that your wives rule over you, for everything that you do and toil for, you take and give to your wives.
And a man girds on his sword and sets out on a long road, and whatever he acquires, whether by robbery, or on the sea, or on rivers,
or whether he meets wild beasts or walks in darkness, when he has stolen and plundered and gone through every hardship, he brings all that he has toiled for to his wife.
For a man loves his wife more than his father and mother.
And many have lost their senses and have fallen into slavery for the sake of their wives.
And many have been given over to destruction; they have perished and killed others, they have gone astray and fallen into great sin because of women.
And do you still not believe me? Does he not have power even over that great diadem on his own head? And no man is permitted to approach it.
And I see the daughter of that concubine of the king, for she sat at the king's right hand,
and she took the diadem off his head and put it on her own head, and struck the king on the cheek.
And yet the king's heart was not angered at this; instead he gaped and gazed at her. If she laughed, he laughed with her too, and if she was sad, the king coaxed her until he had made her cheerful.
And now, O men, how can women not be strong, when they do all this?
At that time the king and the great nobles who were with him began to look at one another.

And Zerubbabel began to speak about truth, and said: O men, are women not strong? Great is the earth, high are the heavens, swiftly runs the sun, for its course is like a vault, like the tent of heaven, and then it immediately flies off and reaches its own place in a single day.
Or is he who made all this not great? Truly, truth is great and stronger than all things.
The whole earth calls upon truth, and the heavens bless truth, and all works shake and tremble before it, and with truth there is no falsehood at all.

Wine is unrighteous, the king is unrighteous, women are unrighteous, all the sons of men are unrighteous, all their works are unrighteous; there is no truth in them, and they perish in their unrighteousness.
But truth stands and endures and is strong forever, and it lives and holds its dominion forever and ever.

And with it there is no partiality, and it never changes at all, but it does righteousness; lawlessness and wickedness are far removed from it. And all the works of truth are pleasing in every way, and no falsehood is found in its judgment.
For truth is the strength of kings, and their authority and wealth, and blessed is the Lord, the God of truth!" And he said this and stopped speaking.
And at that moment the whole assembly cried out with a loud voice and said: "Great is truth, and it prevails, and it is strong!"

Then the king said to him: "Ask whatever you wish, and I will give you more than what is written there, for you have been found wiser than all. And you shall sit next to my throne and be called my kinsman!"
Then Zerubbabel said to the king: "Remember the vow that you made to rebuild Jerusalem on the day you received this royal dignity of yours,

when you said: 'I will return there all the vessels and service-furnishings of Jerusalem, which Cyrus set apart and selected when he overthrew Babylon.' And he vowed to restore that service of the Lord.
So also you, O king, vowed to rebuild the temple of the Lord, which the Edomites burned when the Chaldeans laid Judea waste.

And now I beseech you, my lord the king, and I ask of you that you grant me this great gift. And for this reason I beseech you: fulfil the vow that you made to the King of heaven, and do it just as it came out of your mouth."

Then King Darius rose and kissed Zerubbabel, and he wrote letters for him to all the governors, rulers, commanders and lords, that they should send him and those who were with him on their way to go up and rebuild Jerusalem.

And to all the rulers in the region of Assyria and of Phoenicia, those toward Lebanon, he wrote a letter that they should bring fir wood down from Lebanon to Jerusalem and build the city together with Zerubbabel.

And he wrote on behalf of all the Jews who had gone up out of his kingdom, and he freed them from tribute. And he said to all the mighty men, lords, rulers and governors: "Let no one come to their doors for tribute.
And every place that they hold shall be free and exempt from tribute. And let the Idumeans give back the villages and places of the Jews that they had held.
For the building of the temple, let twenty talents a year be given from the royal treasury until they have built the temple.
And for the altar of burnt offerings, let there be given every day, as it is written in the law, seven and ten [?] offerings to be made without hindrance, and another ten talents a year.
And let all who go up to Jerusalem build the city. And let them be free and exempt from tribute, they themselves and their descendants and all the priests."
And he ordered that all the expenses and the tunics of the priests who carry out the service of the Lord be written down and given.
And for the Levites he wrote down an allowance until the day when they complete the temple of the Lord and Jerusalem is rebuilt.
And for all who guard the city he wrote that they be given an inheritance of land and their wages.

And he sent off all the vessels and service-vessels of the temple which Cyrus had brought out of Babylon. And everything that Cyrus had said and done, he carried out, and he sent all the service-vessels of the Lord to Jerusalem.
And when Zerubbabel came out from the king, he lifted up his hands to heaven, toward Jerusalem, and blessed the Lord, the King of heaven, and said:
"From you comes wisdom, and from you comes strength, and glory is fitting for you, and I am your servant!
I bless you, who gave me wisdom, and I thank you, O God of our fathers!"
And he took the letters and went away. He came to Babylon, went in, and told his brothers.
And they blessed the God of their fathers, because he had granted them relief and release,
so that they might go and build Jerusalem and the temple of the Lord, which was called by his name. And they held a great celebration with all the musicians for seven days.

And after all this, the heads of families and the leaders of the clans' houses were chosen to go up to Jerusalem with their wives, sons and daughters, with their slaves, and with all their goods and bedding.
And Darius sent a thousand horses with them, until they had gone and arrived safely in Jerusalem. With musicians, drums and pipes,
with choral dancing, dancing, and every kind of joy he sent them off to Jerusalem.
And these are the names of the men who went up to Jerusalem, listed by the names of their fathers and by the families of their tribes.

Of the priests there were the sons of Phinehas, son of Aaron: Jeshua son of Jozadak, and Joakim, who was [?] Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, of the line of David, of the tribe of Perez, of the family of Judah,
who had spoken those words of wisdom before King Darius in the second year of his reign, in the month of Nisan, the first month.
And these were all the Jews who were released from captivity and went up to Jerusalem, who had been taken captive by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians.

And they went up to Jerusalem and settled in Judea, each in his own city. Their leaders were Zerubbabel and Jeshua son of Jozadak. And of the priestly family there were: Nehemiah, Sarel, Erese, Ananias, Murtke, Beelsar, Aspharael, Zorovel, Horoim, Gaaza.
And this is the number of the heads of families, of the clans, and of their chiefs: the sons of Parosh, 2,072;
the sons of Phatis, 472; the sons of Aser, 756;
the sons of Nephthalem of Moabel, and of the sons of Jeshua and of Hroab, 2,812;
the sons of Elam, 2,254; the sons of Zattu, 945; the sons of Chorbe, 750; the sons of Badia, 648;
the sons of Begea, 623; the sons of Argea, 3,322;
the sons of Adonikam, 677; the sons of Bosor, 2,606; the sons of Adin, 454;
the sons of Ezir Hezekiah, 92; the sons of Elan and Azate, 67; the sons of Azar, 432; the sons of Gedal, 632;
the sons of Ananias, 120; the sons of Arom, 323; the sons of Arsiphur, 114;
the sons of Beterea, 3,094; the sons of Bethlomia, 123;
From Netophah, fifty-five; from Anathoth, one hundred fifty-eight; from Bethasmoth, forty-two;
from Kiriatharim, twenty-five; from Chephirah and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-eight;
from Chadias and Ammidioi, four hundred twenty-two; from Kirama and Geba, six hundred twenty-one;
from Macalon, one hundred twenty-two; from Betolio, fifty-two; the sons of Niphis, one hundred fifty-six;
the sons of Calamolalus and of Ono, seven hundred twenty-five; the sons of Jerechus, three hundred forty-five;
the sons of Senaah, three thousand three hundred thirty-one.
And the sons of the priests: the sons of Jedaiah, son of Jeshua, nine hundred thirty-two; the sons of Immer, one thousand fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven; the sons of Harim, one thousand seventeen.
And the sons of the Levites: those of Jeshua, one [?], and those of Kadmiel and of Bannas and of Sudias, seventy-four.
And those of the priestly family who were singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred forty-eight.
And the gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Aterara, the sons of Tolmia, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Shobai — all these, one hundred thirty-nine.
And the servants of the priests: the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth, the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon, the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah,
the sons of Akkub, the sons of Uthai, the sons of Ketab, the sons of Hagab, the sons of Subai, the sons of Hanan, the sons of Cathua, the sons of Geddur,

the sons of Airus, the sons of Daisan, the sons of Noeba, the sons of Asab, the sons of Gazera, the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Assan, the sons of Maani, the sons of Naphis, the sons of Akum, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Asur, the sons of Phakis, the sons of Bazluth,
the sons of Dedan, the sons of Kutha, the sons of Charea, the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah, the sons of Nasi, the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Pharida, the sons of Jeeli, the sons of Lozon, the sons of Salia, the sons of Saphuva,

the sons of Hagia, the sons of Phacareth, the sons of Sabie, the sons of Sarothie, the sons of Masia, the sons of Gas, the sons of Addus, the sons of Subas, the sons of Apherra, the sons of Barodis, the sons of Phatis, the sons of Allon —
all the servants of the priests and the servants of Solomon, three hundred seventy-two.
These were the ones who had come up from Babylon, and from Telmelah and Telharsha: their leaders, and Kartalan and Allar.
And no one could count the others, neither by fathers nor by families, as to whether they were of Israel: the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Satubena, the sons of Nekodan — six hundred fifty-two.

Among the priests, those who had served in the priesthood were not found: the sons of Obdia, the sons of Jacob, the sons of Judah, who had taken wives from the daughters of Barzillai and were called by their name.

And they searched for them, and did not find them in the books of the register of the families, in the allotted place [?]; and since they were not found in the register of the families, they were separated and were not admitted to the priesthood.
And Nehemiah and Attharias said to them: "Do not approach the holy things until a high priest arises who is clothed with Manifestation and Truth."

And all Israel, from twelve years old and upward, apart from the male and female servants, was forty-three thousand three hundred sixty; their male and female servants, seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; the singers and attendants, two hundred forty-five.
Camels, four hundred and thirty-five; horses, seven thousand and forty-six; mules, two hundred and forty-five; and donkeys, five thousand five hundred and twenty-five.

And the heads of families, like the heads of their fathers' families, came and entered the site of the temple of God that was in Jerusalem. They made a vow that the temple would be raised again on its own site, according to its proper order.
And they gave money toward the temple to help with what it needed: a thousand talents of gold, three-five [?] thousand talents of silver, and a hundred priestly tunics.
And the priests, the Levites and the people settled in Jerusalem and its surrounding places. The singers, the temple servants, the gatekeepers and all Israel settled in their own villages and fields.
And in the seventh month all the children of Israel set out, each from his own place, and gathered together in the broad open place of the first gate, on the east side.

And Jeshua son of Jozadak took his place with his brothers and the whole body of their priests, and so did Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel with his brothers. They prepared the altar of the Lord God of Israel
so that they could offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the book of Moses, the man of God.

And they gathered and separated themselves from the other nations of that land, and they set up the altar for offerings in its own place. Although those nations were their enemies, all the peoples of that land became their helpers, and they brought gifts as offerings to the altar of the Lord at the appointed times, morning and evening.
And they kept the feast of Tabernacles, as it is written in the law of Moses, and they offered sacrifice every day, as had been commanded.
And after this they offered the burnt offerings at their appointed times, on the sabbaths and the new moons, and they ordered and observed all the holy feasts.
And those who had made vows to God began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord God from the new moon of the seventh month, though the temple of the Lord God had not yet been built.

And they paid wages to the masons and carpenters, and likewise gave provisions to the Sidonians and Tyrians so that they would bring down fir timber. They brought it by ship to the harbour of Joppa, as Cyrus king of the Persians had commanded and ordered them beforehand.

In the second year after they came up to Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began building the temple. With them were their brothers, the chief priests, the Levites, and all who had come out of captivity to Jerusalem.
And they laid the foundation of the house of the Lord God at the new moon of the second month, in the second year after they came up to Judea and Jerusalem.

And they appointed the Levites who were twenty years old and over to be in charge of the work of the Lord's service. Those appointed were Jeshua with his sons and brothers; Kadmiel his brother; the sons of Jeshua, Lema and Bus; and the sons of Jovida son of Eliadun, with their brothers. All the Levites worked together on the work of the house of the Lord.

And the masons, the builders, built the house of the Lord, and the high priests were set in order. They were clothed in the [?] vestment, with musical instruments and trumpets. And the Levites, the sons of Asaph, had cymbals, and they praised, sang and blessed God, as David, king of Israel, had appointed praise with instruments.
And with a loud voice they blessed and gave thanks to the Lord God, for the goodness of God and his glory are upon Israel forever.
With a loud voice all the people blew their trumpets and shouted with a loud voice and blessed God, who had raised up his holy temple.

And the high priests and the Levites came and went in. They were chiefs and leaders according to the headship of their fathers, and they had seen the temple before this building. They came with great weeping
and many trumpets and great joy.
For the multitude could not hear the sound of the trumpet because of the sound of the people's weeping. Though many were blowing the trumpets, the sound reached distant places.
And the enemies of the tribe of Judah and of Benjamin heard the sound. And they came to see and to understand what that sound of the trumpet was.
And they understood that those who had come out of captivity from Babylon were building the temple of the Lord, the God of Israel.
And they approached Zerubbabel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and the other patriarchs and said to them: "Let us build the temple of the Lord."

"As you are, so also are we, the Samaritans." They had been brought from the [?] and the Chaldeans and settled in the places of Galilee belonging to the tribes of Israel, and these were enemies of the tribe of Judah and of Benjamin. "We will obey the Lord your God, for we too have desired this coming forth of yours from the day when Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, carried us captive and brought us and settled us here."
And Zerubbabel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and the other patriarchs of Israel said to them: "It is not lawful for us and for you to build the house of the Lord our God.
We will build the temple of the Lord God, as Cyrus, king of the Persians, commanded us."
For these were the peoples who were associated with the enemies of Judah, who hindered the building in the times of King Cyrus,
for he had commanded them to build the temple during his lifetime.
And after his death they hindered it for twelve years, until the second year of Darius.
And in the second year of King Darius, Haggai and Zechariah prophesied. They prophesied in Judea and Jerusalem in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.

At that time Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak began to build the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem. The prophets of the Lord were with them, and so were those who were helping them.
At that time Sisinnes, governor of the Assyrians and the Phoenicians, and Sathrabuzanes and other companions with them came to them and said to them:
"By whose command are you building this temple and its courts? Or who are those who want it built and completed?"
And the grace of visitation came from the Lord upon the priests and upon Judea,
And they did not stop them from building until word could be written to King Darius and they could receive a command from him.

The letter that they wrote and sent to King Darius: "Sisinnes, governor of Syria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes, and those who are with them, the court officials [?] and rulers of Syria and Phoenicia,

send greetings to King Darius. Let it be known to you, our lord the king, that we went to the land of Judea and entered the city of Jerusalem. There, in the city of Jerusalem, we found the people who had returned from captivity, and their high priests. We saw that they were building the temple of the Lord, very great and wonderful, of very large hewn stones, and they were setting costly [?] timber into its walls.
And that work was being carried forward in their hands with great speed, and with great glory they intended to build it up at once.
Then we asked those elders and said to them: 'By whose command are you building this house? Or by whose word did you lay its foundation?'
And we questioned them so that we might inform you and show you the men who were their leaders, and write down the names of those who were the chiefs of their work.
And they answered us and said to us: 'We are servants of the Lord God, who made the heavens and the earth.
This temple was built long ago by the hand of the great and mighty king of Israel.

But when our fathers provoked and sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth, he gave them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who was king of the Chaldeans.
In the first year of the reign of Cyrus in Babylon, King Cyrus wrote and commanded that this temple be built.

And all the vessels and service implements of this temple, of gold and silver, which King Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from the house of the Lord in Jerusalem and placed in the house of his idols — afterwards Cyrus brought them out of that house of the idols of the Babylonians and gave them to Zerubbabel and Sanabassar.
And he commanded them to take those vessels and service implements and place them in the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem. And he commanded that the temple be built on its site.
Then Sanabassar went up to Jerusalem and laid the foundation of this temple. From that time until now we have been building, and it is not yet finished.'
And now, our lord King Darius, have a search made and look in the house of the chronicles, where the books of records of King Cyrus are kept stored,

and if it is found that they are building the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem by the command and by the word of King Cyrus, then give heed to the command of King Cyrus, and inform us about this whole matter!"

Then King Darius ordered a search in the house of the royal chronicles, which was in Babylon. And in Btan of Bariten [?], in the village of Marta [?], it was found — in the place where the book of records lay — in which it was written thus:
"In the first year of the reign of Cyrus, King Cyrus commanded that the house of the Lord in Jerusalem be built, where they would offer sacrifices openly by means of fire.

And he commanded this form of measurement for the building: its height sixty cubits and its breadth sixty cubits, and to lay three courses of hewn stone and one course of new timber; and all the expenses were commanded to be paid from the royal treasury.

And the vessels for the service of the house of the Lord, of gold and of silver, which Nebuchadnezzar had carried off to Babylon from the temple of the Lord that was in Jerusalem, King Cyrus commanded to be taken back to the house of the Lord that was in Jerusalem, so that they might place them there as it had been before.

And King Darius added further to that command and said: "Sisinnes, governor of the Assyrians and the Phoenicians, and Sathrabuzanes, and your other companions, who are appointed over the affairs of the Assyrians and the Phoenicians: keep away from that place, and do not approach that servant of the Lord, Zerubbabel, who is governor of the Jews, nor the chief priests of the Jews, who together are building that house in its own place.
I have commanded that it be built completely and entirely; and I am a helper to those Jews who have gone up to Jerusalem, until they complete that temple of the Lord, their God.

And from the tributes of the region of Assyria and of Phoenicia I have ordered by decree that they be given to those men for the offerings of the Lord. And let Zerubbabel the governor take [?] bullocks and rams and lambs,

and in the same manner wheat and salt, wine and oil; and let all of this be appointed year by year. As much as the priests in Jerusalem shall order for the service of the Lord, let it be given day by day without hindrance,
so that they may offer sacrifice to the Lord their God and pray for the life of the king."

And he commanded: "If anyone is negligent, or transgresses this command of mine which I have written, let him be punished and pay for all this with his own head, and let him be hung up and flogged, and let all his property be taken for the royal treasury.

For wherever the name of the Lord is invoked, there all royal and national care was commanded; and he [who] dared to stretch out a hand and to hinder, and devised evil against the temple that is in Jerusalem [?]...
I, King Darius, have commanded with great diligence that all of this be done and accomplished."

Then Sisinnes, the great governor, who was over the region of Assyria and Phoenicia, and Sathrabuzanes and their other companions, who had been hindering the work of the temple, when they received the command from King Darius,
began to oversee and took care of the work, and became fellow workers with the elders of the Jews and the chief priests.
And the work of that temple prospered, for Haggai and Zechariah were prophesying.
And they completed that temple according to the command of the Lord, the God of Israel,

and according to the command and will of Cyrus and Darius, in the sixth year of King Darius. That holy temple was completed [?] on the twentieth, the third [i.e. twenty-third?] of the month Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of Darius.

And the sons of Israel, the priests, the Levites and all those who had come out of captivity did so. The holy temple was completed in the month of Mihrakan, on the twenty-fifth of the month. Its building took forty-six years: thirty years under Cyrus, nine under Kaise, one year under Artaxerxes, six years under the Magi, and with Darius, forty-six years in all. This was as it had been ordained and commanded in the books of the law of Moses.
And they offered the dedication sacrifice of the house of the Lord: a hundred bulls, two hundred rams and four hundred lambs,
and twelve yearlings for the sins of all Israel, according to the number of the heads of the tribes of Israel.

And the priests and the Levites were arranged by their families, and the [?] was assigned to them before the Lord, the God of Israel, as it is commanded in the books of Moses. And the gatekeepers were placed at each gate.
And the sons of Israel who had come out of captivity kept the Passover of the Lord on the fifteenth day of the first month, for the priests and the Levites had been purified, all of them together,
those who had come out of captivity. And when the Levites had been purified,
they kept the Passover of the Lord for all the sons of Israel who had come out of captivity, for their brothers and for the priests themselves.
And the sons of Israel who had come out of their captivity ate it, all those who had separated themselves from the defilement of the gentiles and who sought the Lord God.
And they kept the feast of unleavened bread for seven days, and they rejoiced before the Lord,
for God had turned the mind of the king of the Assyrians toward them and strengthened their hands for the work of the Lord, the God of Israel.

And when all this had been completed, King Artaxerxes took the crown over the Persians. Ezra came to him. Ezra was the son of Azariah, who was descended from Jezeriah, who was descended from Hilkiah, who was descended from Shallum,

who was descended from Zadok, who was descended from Ahitub, who was descended from Amariah. This is Artaxerxes Longimanus ("the Long-handed"), who helped Ezra and honored him in every rite and in everything needed for the departure of the Jews. Amariah was descended from Iozek, who was descended from Meraioth, who was descended from Zerahiah, who was descended from Seuse, who was descended from Bukki, who was descended from Abishua, who was descended from Eleazar, who was descended from Aaron, the first priest.
This Ezra went up from Babylon. He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which was given by God to Israel.
And the king gave him glory. Ezra found favor before him, and the king honored him greatly.

And with him some of the sons of Israel went up to Jerusalem, along with some of the priests, the Levites and the servants, the psalm-singers and the gatekeepers, and some of the servants of the priests. They went in the seventh year of the reign of King Artaxerxes, in the fifth month; that was the king's seventh year.
They left Babylon at the beginning of the first month, and at the beginning of the fifth month they entered Jerusalem, because the Lord gave them success.
For Ezra was full of all wisdom, and he lacked nothing of all the commandments of the Lord. He taught Israel judgments and righteous decrees according to the law.
The letter of command from King Artaxerxes reached Ezra the priest, who explained the law of the Lord. And the king wrote as follows:
"King Artaxerxes to Ezra, the priest and reader of the law: greetings.

Out of complete benevolence I have decided, and I command, that all of the Jewish people who wish to go up to Jerusalem, and the chief priests and the Levites, may go with you to Jerusalem without fear.
And since they eagerly wish to go to Judea and Jerusalem, I and my seven counsellors have commanded
that they go according to the law and carry out everything.

And let them offer the offering to the Lord, the God of Israel, as I and my friends vowed in Jerusalem. And let all the gold and silver, as much as may be found in the land of the Babylonians, be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord God in Jerusalem.
And take the contribution [?] from the land of the Babylonians: let them bring to the priests of the Lord God in Jerusalem gold and silver, bullocks and rams and lambs.
And let all the other dedicated offerings of the sacrifices be offered to the Lord God in Jerusalem.
And do whatever you and your brothers wish. As for the gold and silver from the tributes, use it according to the will of the Lord your God.
And take the sacred vessels and the utensils for the service to Jerusalem, and let them be used as the temple of the Lord God needs them, and set them all before the Lord your God in Jerusalem.
And whatever surplus and remainder is left over from the needs of the temple, deposit it in the royal treasury.

And I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded the treasurers who are in Assyria and in the region of the Canaanites that whatever Ezra, the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, God Most High, wishes to receive is to be given to him without hindrance, up to a hundred talents of silver,
and likewise a hundred measures of wheat, and the same amount of wine and oil.
And let them receive everything according to the law and render it to the Lord, God Most High, so that the wrath of the Lord may not come upon my majesty and upon my son's.

And I have commanded you concerning the priests and the Levites, the psalm-singers, the ministers and the gatekeepers, and the servants of the priests and the ministers of the house of the Lord: let no one have authority to take from them any tribute or anything else at all.

And you, Ezra, according to your wisdom, which has been given to you by God, appoint overseers and judges to judge throughout the region of Assyria and Phoenicia. And as for all those who have learned the law of the Lord your God, and those who have not learned it, teach them.

And as for all who transgress the law of the Lord your God and the law of us, the kings: I have given you authority to punish and to flog them; and if they deserve death, to put them to death; or if they deserve punishment, to punish them and to exact a fine."
And Ezra, the scribe of the law of the Lord, said: "Blessed is the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put all this into the king's heart, to glorify this temple of the Lord which is in Jerusalem.
And he made me glorious and honoured before his majesty, before all his counsellors and friends and all his nobles.
I rejoiced greatly through the help of the Lord our God." And he gathered all the men of Israel who had gone up with him to Jerusalem.

And these are the heads of the clans, according to their fathers' houses and according to the divisions of their fathers and kindred, who came up with Ezra from Babylon in the reign of King Artaxerxes:
Of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Gamael; of the sons of David, Pharez;
of the sons of Phoros, Zechariah, and with him those who were registered, a hundred and fifty men;
of the sons of Pahath-moab, Eliaonias son of Zareas, and with him two hundred men;
of the sons of Zathoes, Jezonias son of Jetherias, and with him three hundred men; of the sons of Adin, Jonathan, and with him two hundred and fifty men;
of the sons of Elam, [?] of Gotholias, and with him seventy men;
of the sons of Shephatiah, Zechariah son of Michael, and with him seventy men;
of the sons of Joab, Abdias son of Ezel, and with him two hundred and twelve men;
of the sons of Bani, Assalimoth son of Saphe, and with him a hundred and sixty men;
of the sons of Beri, Zechariah son of Abibe, and with him twenty-eight men;
of the sons of Astath, Johanan son of Katai, and with him a hundred and ten men;
of the sons of Adonikam and of Esphat, and these are their names: Eliphat, Geluvel, and Sameas, and with them seventy men;
of the sons of Bene, Uthias son of Takur, and with him seventy men.
And he gathered them at the bank of the river called Thera, and they pitched camp there for only three days, and they made an inspection of all the sons.
Of the sons of the priests and of the sons of the Levites, no one was found among them.
And I sent for Eleazar, and there came to me Sameas, Oribon, Nathan, Ennatar, Zechariah, and Mosollobon. These are leaders and teachers of the law.
And I told them to go to Lodeon, the chief of the treasurers.
And I commanded them to tell Lodeon and his brothers, and those who were with them at the place of the treasury, to send us some of the priests for the house of the Lord.

And they brought to us men who were strong according to the word of the Lord and knowledgeable in the law of the Lord: of the son of Mooli, who was of Levi and of Israel, Aserevian, and his sons and brothers, twelve;
and Asebian and Aunon and Osetan, a brother, of the sons of Kanuz, and his sons, twenty men;
and of the servants of the priests, whom David the ruler gave for the work of the service of the Levites, whose names were written down as notable men, twenty.
And there we proclaimed a fast and prayed before the Lord our God,
and we asked for an easy way and success for ourselves and for our children and for everything that was with us.
For it seemed burdensome to us to ask the king for footmen [?] and horsemen to go with us on the way, to help us against those who opposed us;
for we had said to the king thus: "The power of the Lord our God is with us and with all who seek him."
And there, on behalf of all of them, we proclaimed a fast and prayed that the Lord would protect us and guide us on the ways of peace.
And I chose from the leaders of the families and of the priests Esebias and Esemias, and with them ten men from among their brethren.

And we weighed out and gave them the gold and silver, the priestly service vessels and the vessels of the house of the Lord, which the king, his counsellors, his princes and all their assembly had given us.

I weighed out and gave the silver, six hundred and fifty talents; silver service vessels, a hundred talents; and a hundred talents of gold. There were also twenty other vessels of gold, and twelve vessels of bronze, holy, choice and gold-coloured.

And I said to them: "You are sanctified by the Lord, and all the service vessels of gold and silver are holy and belong to the Lord. Pray to the Lord, and may the Lord, the God of our fathers, protect us and bring us in peace to this place of his holiness."
"Stay watchful and guard them until you bring them and deliver them to the chiefs of the priests and of the Levites, and to the rulers, the chiefs of Israel, who are in Jerusalem."
So the keepers of the temple of the Lord, the chief priests and the Levites, took the silver, the gold and the service vessels, to receive them into the temple of the Lord that is in Jerusalem.

And we arose and set out from the river Thera on the twelfth day of the first month. We came and arrived at Jerusalem in the month [?], protected by the exalted and mighty arm of God. The Lord our God delivered us from all our enemies, and we arrived at Jerusalem alive and in peace.
After we had rested in Jerusalem for only three days, on the fourth day we weighed out the silver and gold and gave it, for the house of the Lord, to the priest Marmoth, of the Jews [?],

and to those who were with him: Eleazar son of Phinehas, Josabad son of Jeshua, Moeth [?] son of Saben, and other Levites. We gave it to them by weight and by number, and the full weight and count was found correct that same day.

And those who had come out with us from the Babylonian captivity offered sacrifice to the Lord, the God of Israel: twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety rams, seventy-five lambs, and twelve goats as a sin offering. They offered all these offerings before the Lord God.

And they delivered the document containing the king's command to the king's officials and to the rulers and governors of Assyria and Phoenicia. And our nation and the temple of the Lord were glorified with great honour.
When all this had been completed, the nobles and chiefs of the sons of Israel came before me and said:

"The whole nation of the sons of Israel has not kept itself separate. Their leaders, priests and Levites have mixed with the gentiles and foreigners and with the abominations of all the foreign peoples: the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Moabites, Amorites, Egyptians and Edomites.

"For they have defiled themselves with their daughters, both they and their sons, and their holy seed has been mixed with the foreigners and gentiles of that land. The leaders and the great men have each, of their own accord, become lawless, for they have been the leaders in this evil intermixing."
And it came to pass, when I heard these words, that I tore my garments and lamented, and I pulled out the hair of my head and my beard, and I sat mourning, deeply grieved.

And when they heard my lamentation, which was for the Lord, the God of Israel, everyone gathered around me. And they saw what I was doing over their iniquities, for I sat grieving like this until evening, until the time of the evening offering came.
And I rose up from that mourning, with my garment still torn, and I was downcast with great mourning. And I lifted up my hands to the Lord my God, cried out, and said:
"Lord, we are ashamed and we tremble before your face,
for our sins have grown more numerous than the hairs of our head, and our iniquities have risen higher than the heavens,
from the years and times of our fathers, and we have remained in great sins to this very day.

And because of our sins and those of our fathers, we were given over to captivity: we and our brothers and our kings and our high priests. And all the kings of the earth surrounded us; they took us captive by the edge of the sword and laid waste our places, and we have been put to shame to this very day and in those times.
And now, Lord, how great your mercy has been, to leave a root and a people in the place of your holiness,
and you made a light shine in the temple of the Lord our God, and you gave us food in the time of our servitude

and in that captivity. You did not cast us out of your hands, but you, Lord, became our helper, and you let us find favour before the king of the Persians. You honoured us and provided for us with every provision,
and he glorified the temple of the Lord our God, and he raised up and rebuilt desolate Zion, and he settled us in Judea and Jerusalem.
And now, Lord, what shall I say before you about all this? For we have transgressed your law and your commandments, Lord, which you gave us by the hand of your servants the prophets, when you said:
'The land that you are entering to possess is a land defiled by the pollution of the peoples of that land, and they have filled it with their defilement.
And now, do not take wives for your son from among their daughters, and do not give any of your daughters as wives to their sons;
and do not ever make peace with them, so that you may be strong and eat the richness of that land. And you shall leave that land to your sons as an inheritance for all ages.'
And what has happened to us has happened because of the wickedness of our sins.
But you, Lord, have forgiven our sins many times and given us such a people and root. Yet we turned away again and transgressed your law, and we mixed with the uncleanness of the people of that land.
Even so, have you not held back until now from becoming angry with us to the point of destroying us, so that no root, seed or name of ours would remain?
You are righteous, Lord, God of Israel, and true. You did not wipe out our people, and we have remained as a root and seed to this very day.
And now, behold, we stand before you today in our iniquities, and we cannot stand before your face, for our iniquities and our wickednesses have multiplied beyond the hairs of our heads."

And while Ezra was praying with that confession and with great lamentation, he lay prostrate, face down on the ground, before the temple of the Lord. All who were in Jerusalem gathered to him, a great crowd: fathers and mothers, young men and maidens, for the lamentation of that multitude of people was great.

And Jechoniah, one of the sons of Israel, made a proposal [?] and said: "Ezra, we have sinned against the Lord our God, and we have taken wives from the foreigners of that land, and now, today, there are iniquities among us.

And now let us all come and take an oath before the Lord, and let us put away from us our wives whom we took from the foreigners, together with their children, as the law of the Lord our God commands.
Rise at once and carry it out, for all our affairs rest with you, and we are with you. Whatever you command, we will do!"
And Ezra rose and made the chiefs of the tribes of the priests and of the Levites, and all Israel, swear to act in this manner, and they swore.
And Ezra rose from the court of the temple of the Lord and went to the house of John and of Elisabean.
And he stayed there; he ate no bread and drank no water, and he mourned over those iniquities and the great multitude of their sins.
And a herald made proclamation throughout all Judea and Jerusalem. And all those who had come out of the captivity came and gathered at Jerusalem.

And after two or three days, those who did not arrive there were judged by the leaders and the elders, and they plundered their possessions, and those who had become estranged they expelled from the multitude of the people of the captivity.
And all who were of the tribe of Judah and of Benjamin gathered at Jerusalem within three days, in the ninth month, on the twentieth day of the month.
And all that multitude sat with him in the open space of the court of the house of the Lord, and they trembled, frozen by the severity of the winter.
And Ezra rose and said: "You are the ones who have sinned and taken wives from the daughters of the foreigners, and you have added to the iniquity and sin of Israel.
And now make confession to the Lord, the God of our fathers,
and do his will, and separate yourselves from all the gentiles of the land and from the foreign wives whom you have taken."
And all that multitude together cried out with a loud voice and said: "We will do just as you have said.

But this season is winter, and we are very many, and we cannot endure the hardship of this winter like this. And this matter is not a work of one day or two days, for we have sinned very greatly in this matter.
Now let the chiefs and leaders stand over this multitude, and let all who have a foreign woman in their house come and be assigned [?] a time.
And in each place let the elders and the judges stand and give relief [?], and turn away from us the wrath of the Lord for the very great wickednesses that we have committed."
Jonathan son of Azael and Hezekiah son of Thocanus took it upon themselves to do this, and Mosollamus and Levi and Sabbateus, who were in agreement with them.
And those who had come out of the captivity did everything just as they had been commanded.
And Ezra chose men who were priests, rulers and heads of fathers' houses, each by name. And they sat down on the first day of the tenth month to carry out the matter.
And they gathered and brought the fathers and mothers who had taken wives of foreign stock, until the first month.
And among the priests who had been gathered, some were found who had taken wives of foreign stock and had mixed with the ungodly:
of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak, and of his brother Mathelas: Eleazar and Joribus and Joadan.
And they began to put away their foreign wives, and each of them offered rams as atonement for sins of ignorance.
And of the sons of Immer: Hananiah and Baddius and Mannes and Sammeas and Jeriel and Azariah.
And of the sons of Pashhur: Elianas and Massias, Ishmael and Nathanael, Uketledus and Salthus.
And of the sons of the Levites: Jazaptus and Semis and Conius, that is, Salvitas, and Patheus, who was also called Judah, and Jonas.
Of the psalm-singers who served: Eliashib and Bacchurus.
Of the gatekeepers: Salomius and Tolbanes.
And of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Jeramus and Jeddius and Melchias and Males and Eleazar and Sabias and Baneas.
And of the sons of Eliakim: Mattanias, Zacharias, Jezorieliel [?], Jobadius and Jerimoth and Jedius.
And of the sons of Zattu: Eliadas and Elisimus, Othonias, Arimoth and Sabathus and Zarde.
And of the sons of Bebai: Johannes and Ananias and Jozabus and Emaoz.
And of the sons of Eman: Eulamus, Mamumus, Jedeus, Jasobus, Jasaelus and Jaremoth.
And of the sons of Addi: Nathus and Moosias, Lacunus, Naidas and Tatias and Sesthes and Balunus and Manasses.
And of the sons of Ananias: Elionas and Aseas and Melchias and Sabeus and Simon and Chosameus.
And of the sons of Asomat: Annesus and Mattathias and Baneus and Eliphatal and Manasses and Semeis.

And of the sons of Balam: Jeremias, Momdis, Maerus and Joel, Mambdes and Perdias and Anos, Rabasion and Anasibus and Mamnetanemus, Eliasis and Shimei and Selemias and Nathanias. And of the sons of Ezora: Esis, Ezriel, Azil, Samaton and Zambris, Joseph.
And of the sons of Naum: Zazikias, Zabadias, Edesioel, Benesias.
All these had taken wives of foreign stock, and they put away their wives and their children.
And the priests and the Levites and Israel settled in Jerusalem and in the villages on the first day of the seventh month, and the sons of Israel settled in their own dwellings.
And the whole multitude gathered together in the broad open place on the east side, in front of the gate of the temple,
and they told Ezra, the high priest and reader of the law, to bring the law of Moses, which had been given by the Lord, the God of Israel.
And Ezra brought the law out into the midst, before all the men and women and before all the priests, and they heard the law of the Lord at the new moon of the seventh month.

And he read the book at the gate of the temple, in the broad place, from dawn until the sixth hour, before all the men and women, and the whole multitude listened to the law of the Lord God and understood it.
And Ezra, the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, stood on a wooden platform that had been prepared.
Standing near him were, on the right side, Mattathias, Sammus, Ananias, Azarias, Urias, Ezekias, and Baalsamus,
and on the left side Phaldaius and Misael, Malchias, Lothasubus, Nabarias, and Zacharias.
And Ezra took the book of the law in his hands, for he sat in great glory before everyone, and the whole multitude sat before him.
And when he unrolled the books of the law, the whole multitude stood up, and Ezra blessed the Lord, God Most High, God of Sabaoth and Almighty.
And the whole multitude said together, "Amen." And they lifted up their hands to heaven, fell to the ground on their faces, and worshipped the Lord God.

And Jeshua and Anniuth and Sarabias, Iadinus, Iacubus, Sabbateus, Auteas, Maiannas and Calitas, Azarias and Jozabdus and Ananias, and Biatas: these were the Levites who taught the people the law of the Lord, made them understand it, and [?] them in the law of the Lord God.
And Attharates [?] spoke to Ezra, the priest and reader of the law of the Lord, and to the Levites who were teaching the multitude; he spoke to them before everyone:
"This day is a day holy to the Lord, and all are undone by hearing the law of the Lord."
"Go, eat rich food and drink sweet drink, and send [?] (the text reads 'a book/letter') to those who have nothing,"
"for this day is holy to the Lord. Do not distress them, for it is the Lord God who has glorified us."
And all the Levites gave orders to the whole multitude and said: "This day is holy; do not distress them."
And they said to the multitude: "Whoever has something, let him eat and drink and be merry, and let them give to those who have nothing." And everyone was very merry that day.
For we were filled and understood the words of the Lord our God, the words of the law of the Lord God, in which you gathered and taught us.
